title: Hit Vibes cover art
lede: Saint Pepsi’s 2013 cover imitates an early-1980s record sleeve: a red square, floating parallelograms, a yellow wedge, and a thin swoosh on grainy grey.
summary: Mock-1980s sleeve: red square, drop-shadowed parallelograms, yellow wedge, grey grain. 2013.

evidence.note: Inspected the 900 × 900 front cover in the [Cover Art Archive](https://musicbrainz.org/release/ff881a14-c23e-4728-bfb9-7b11bb5b6ecd/cover-art), in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.

styles.note: Partial fit, from the future-funk branch: it quotes 1980s commercial graphics, the [Memphis](style:memphis)-derived shapes Wikipedia lists among the style’s sources, but has no pastel gradient, statue, or digital chrome.

context: Wikipedia names Skylar Spence (formerly Saint Pepsi) among the most popular future funk artists, and lists Saint Pepsi among the performers at the first vaporwave festival in 2019. [Wikipedia: Vaporwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaporwave).
observed: A large red square with a thin black outline sits on a grey, grainy ground.
A row of small red parallelograms with grey drop shadows crosses the top diagonally; a thin yellow wedge cuts down through the square.
A thin navy swoosh curves across the middle; HIT VIBES is printed faintly inside the square in large outline letters, and SAINT PEPSI in white thin italic capitals at the top left.
interpretation: Useful as a boundary case: it quotes the same 1980s source material as vaporwave through graphic pastiche, without the collage and digital artefacts.

rights.statement: Copyrighted album art. No image is stored here.
